title: rwst/Confinement-Certificates
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper on the emptiness theory of the sets Z_{p/q}(s, s+t) = {ξ > 0 : {ξ(p/q)ⁿ} ∈ [s, s+t) for all n ≥ 0}, the generalized Z-numbers of Flatto, Lagarias and Pollington, at and beyond the window length 1/p. The paper introduces block certificates --- finite integer witnesses, rechecked from scratch by the Lean proof kernel, whose soundness rests on the aperiodicity lemma alone --- and uses them to pass the length-$1/p$ line: $\Zset_{3/2}(1/6,13/24)=\emptyset$ (window length $3/8>1/3$), $\Zset_{3/2}(961/3600,2427/3600)=\emptyset$ (length $733/1800$), and explicit unions of total length up to $17/24$, against $20/39$ in print. The closed-interval union statement of Dubickas is replicated exactly as printed; no $\xi\ne0$ keeps $\|\xi(3/2)^{n}\|<1/5$ for every $n$, with $\|\cdot\|$ the distance to the nearest integer; and thirty windows of length $1/p$ are certified at five bases in the regime $p>q^{2}$ that Dubickas leaves open. There is no sorry anywhere outside the deliberate placeholders in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and no native_decide: every block certificate is discharged by `c.ok = true := by decide`, i.e. by kernel reduction of integer arithmetic on the certificate's raw data.
authors: Claude Code, claude-fable-5 (mathematical discovery, paper drafting)
